titulo: How Google, Bing, and AI find a website
lead: Writing more pages won't help if the search engine can't read the ones you already have. This lesson shows the path a page takes until it appears in a search or an AI answer, the three principles of the inemaSEO method, and Google's official 2026 yardstick for telling foundation from fad.
objetivo: explain the path of crawling, indexing, showing, and citing, and choose what to do first on your site.

aprende.t: The path of a page to search and AI answers
The three principles of the inemaSEO method
What Google's May 2026 guide says about AI
Run the first question test on your topic

hero_alt: A person seen from behind in a large, organized library, looking at long shelves with card files.

secoes.sub: Four steps, always in this order. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: The search engine's bot visits the address and reads the HTML the server delivers. It reaches the page through a link or the sitemap. A page with no links and outside the sitemap is almost never visited.

After reading, the search engine decides whether to keep the page in its index. It can refuse: duplicate address, thin page, or a canonical pointing somewhere else. This is where the technical foundation matters.
Only an indexed page appears in the results. Search Console and Bing Webmaster count how many times it was shown (impression) and clicked.
Google's AI features start from Google's index; Copilot, from Bing's index. For ChatGPT, a study by Seer found most citations among the top Bing results; that's a study, not a statement from OpenAI.

secoes.volta: What doesn't show up goes back to the X-ray: measure and fix
secoes.legenda: There's no shortcut that skips a step: AI cites what search engines can read and store.

secoes.titulo: The three principles and the 2026 yardstick

texto: Without the right canonical, and with the sitemap and robots.txt undecided, no new page pays off. That's why this whole course comes before writing.
You start by looking at what already exists, not by creating more.

exemplo.texto: On 09/23/2026, the /cursos/ page showed up as "Discovered – currently not indexed" and the new pages were unknown to Google.

texto: Every page rests on a course, project, event, or experiment that actually exists. AI can rewrite and organize; it never makes up facts.
This is what Google itself calls non-commodity content: your own experience, which an AI would not produce on its own.

exemplo.texto: If you swap the topic of the page and the paragraph is still valid, it's generic. Rewrite it with something of your own.

texto: People who already search for you by name don't prove your SEO works. The number that matters is people who didn't know you and found you.
At the start, almost every click is from the brand, and that is misleading.

exemplo.texto: In the 28 days from 08/25 to 09/21/2026, 639 of 647 clicks were branded.

texto: Google's official guide to AI features (May/2026) says there is no special requirement to appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode: standard SEO best practices apply.
It also says you don't need to create a file for AI or any special schema. Use this yardstick whenever someone sells you a shortcut.

exemplo.texto: Technical foundation + content with your own experience. The rest is a fad until proven otherwise.

secoes.titulo: The first test: fixed questions on your topic
secoes.sub: Copy the spreadsheet and the questions. Replace what's between < > with your own.

blocos.conteudo:
1. Where can I learn <your topic> in <your city or language>?
2. What is the best way to <problem your business solves>?
3. What is <your business name>?

date;assistant;question;did my site appear? (yes/no);who was cited
<mm/dd/yyyy>;<ChatGPT>;1;no;<cited site>
<mm/dd/yyyy>;<Perplexity>;1;no;<cited site>

abas.html:
A single round on 07/10/2026, with 20 frozen questions: INEMA appeared in 0 of 48 neutral answers on Claude and in 0 of 4 on Gemini. ChatGPT and Perplexity were not measured.

"What is INEMA?" got 4 of 4 answers about a different agency with the same name: a name collision. Question 3 in the spreadsheet exists to catch this in your case.

• Answers vary from one day to the next: write down the date and repeat it the same way next month.
  • Zero today is a starting point, not a failure.
  • The full measurement (20 to 30 questions, every month) is in course 4.

secoes.sub: The 10/10/2026 video walks through all 10 steps. Right below, what the October research corrected.

secoes.titulo: What has changed since the video
secoes.sub: Three statements from the video that the 2026 yardstick adjusts.
paragrafos: llms.txt. The video calls it a "site map for AIs". An Ahrefs study of 137 thousand domains (06/15/2026) found 97% of the files had no requests at all, and Google says it may ignore it. In this course it is optional and cheap (lesson 6).

robots.txt. The video says to allow the AI bots. That is still right, but in 2026 the decision is by purpose: search, user action, and training are different bots, and blocking training doesn't take you out of search (lesson 6).
40-to-60-word answer. A direct answer at the start helps the reader. No source backs it as a technique for being cited by AI; treat it as clarity.

secoes.sub: Two short exercises. Keep your answers: you will come back to them in course 4.

exercicios.texto: Write the 3 test questions for your topic and run each one on two AI assistants. Fill in the spreadsheet.
exercicios.pronto: the spreadsheet has 6 rows with the date, the assistant, and whether your site appeared.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · What only you can say
exercicios.texto: List in 3 lines what your site has of its own: a data point, an experience, a case, a product only you sell.
exercicios.pronto: each line points to a page on your site or to something that could become a page.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: A page is "discovered, but not indexed." Can it show up in a Google AI answer?
opcoes: Yes, AI reads any published page.
No: Google's AI features start from the index, and the page isn't in it yet.
Yes, if it has an llms.txt.
perguntas.explica: The path is crawl, index, show, and cite. Without the index there is no result and no citation. llms.txt doesn't change that: Google says it may ignore it.

perguntas.p: What does Google's May 2026 guide say about appearing in AI Overviews?
opcoes: It requires a special schema for AI.
It requires a text file for AI.
There's no special requirement: SEO best practices and non-commodity content apply.
perguntas.explica: The guide says you don't need a special file or markup. What counts in the long run is content with your own experience. Anyone selling a shortcut is selling a fad.

perguntas.p: Why does the total number of clicks mislead you at the start?
opcoes: Because Search Console gets the math wrong.
Because almost every click comes from people already searching for your name.
perguntas.explica: At INEMA, 639 of 647 clicks were branded. What shows whether SEO is working is non-branded searches, from people who didn't know you.

perguntas.p: The link between ChatGPT and the Bing index is:
opcoes: A hint from a Seer study with a small sample; it's not an OpenAI statement.
A myth with no data at all.
perguntas.explica: The study found most citations among Bing's top results. That's a good reason to look after Bing, but always say where the information comes from.

itens.texto: Crawl → index → show → cite. AI cites what search engines can read and store.
Foundation before content, only real data, measured without the brand.
No special requirement for AI. llms.txt and "40–60 words" are not citation levers.
